content.value_statement: Agent behavior often fails when context is poorly structured or overloaded. This skill explains context components, limits, and practical design patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explains the main parts of model context, including prompts, tools, documents, history, and outputs.
Describes why context windows and attention limits affect agent reliability.
Introduces progressive disclosure for loading information only when needed.
Provides guidance for context budgeting and compaction thresholds.
Shows simple examples for organizing prompts and loading documents progressively.
limitations: It is conceptual guidance, not an automated context management tool.
It does not measure token usage or inspect a live project.
It does not include executable scripts or reusable libraries.
It assumes the user already has an agent or prompt design task.

use_cases.title: Plan an Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Use the skill to decide which context should load at startup and which context should load later.

use_cases.title: Debug Poor Agent Responses
use_cases.description: Use the concepts to check whether message history, tool outputs, or long documents are weakening task focus.

use_cases.title: Teach Context Basics
use_cases.description: Use the skill as a short primer for teams learning context windows, attention budgets, and prompt organization.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Context Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main components of context in an agent system. Use this skill and keep the answer suitable for a new team member.

prompt_templates.title: Review My Prompt Structure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my system prompt structure using this skill. Identify missing sections, overloaded areas, and clearer boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design Progressive Disclosure
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a progressive disclosure plan for my agent. Separate startup context, on-demand documents, and tool outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Context Budget Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my context budgeting strategy for a long-running agent. Cover attention placement, compaction triggers, and degradation planning.

output_examples.input: Explain why my agent loses focus after many tool calls.
output_examples.output: A focused explanation that links tool output growth to context pressure, then suggests compaction and selective retention.

output_examples.input: Help me decide what my agent should load at startup.
output_examples.output: A staged context plan that separates persistent rules, lightweight summaries, and task-specific documents.

output_examples.input: Review this agent design for context risks.
output_examples.output: A concise review covering prompt placement, document loading, message history growth, and degradation planning.

best_practices: Load only high-signal context needed for the current task.
Place critical instructions near attention-favored positions.
Set compaction triggers before context becomes overloaded.
anti_patterns: Loading every document at startup without a task-specific reason.
Treating larger context windows as a complete memory solution.
Ignoring tool output growth during long agent workflows.

faq.question: What does this skill teach?
faq.answer: It teaches how context works in agent systems and why careful context design improves reliability.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown reference skill and does not include executable automation.

faq.question: Is this useful for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The concepts apply to agent systems that depend on prompts, tools, files, and message history.

faq.question: Can it optimize my context automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance that you can apply when designing or reviewing an agent workflow.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before designing prompts, tool definitions, retrieval flows, or long-running agent sessions.

faq.question: What should I read next?
faq.answer: Follow with skills about context degradation, context optimization, multi-agent patterns, or tool design.
